# FND-01 round-one correction evidence

Author: implementation sub-agent, `gpt-6.1-sol` / `max` (T3 runtime). Date: 2026-10-17. This is a bounded correction candidate, **not independent acceptance** of FND-01 or M0. Coordinator inspection, shared-contract reconciliation and fresh non-author Astra xhigh plus separate Sol 6.1 max reviews remain pending.

Starting HEAD was verified as `322d419cb1e8e921fa6fc1e10c2ef8296693c993`, with a clean worktree on `t3/fnd-01-round-one-fixes`, exclusively at `/home/worker/.t3/worktrees/subnautica-clone/t3-de8b807f`. Production source matched the reviewed FND baseline; parent documentation recorded the initial reviews. Correction source commit: **79423ec8a82fe222e36c2311db127a8b41c1f519**. This report is committed separately as evidence bookkeeping after that source commit; no production changes follow it.

## Corrections and scope

- **FND-A1:** Vite alone changes from pinned 7.3.1 to 7.3.7. The regenerated lock changes that package's version, integrity and declared esbuild compatibility range; it does not upgrade other installed packages. Fresh installation and production checks pass.
- **FND-A2 / FND-SOL-01:** a refused initial write now offers **Use without local saving** for New Game or a validated import. Existing-session replacement still has its usual confirmation, followed by this separate explicit choice after an eligible storage/coordination failure. Cancelling either choice retains the active expedition. Accepting the fallback creates an exportable session, leaves local records unchanged and disables autosave. Menu and HUD show the warning; explicit Save locally can retry. Failed manual/autosaves retain active progress and export, and stop automatic retries.
- **FND-A3 / FND-SOL-02:** the stale comparison, preservation checks, journal construction and single `setItem` run within one exclusive browser Web Lock. Every repository uses `siltwake.save.journal.v1.writer` on the origin. Missing or failed safe exclusion never falls back to racing writes. Validation, conflicts, protected records and size refusals have separate failure codes; these refusals do not offer an unsaved replacement shortcut.
- Asynchronous session operations have one pending owner and an abort signal. Conflicting actions and repeated per-frame autosaves deduplicate. Each write has a consistent snapshot. Cancel/dispose invalidates delayed file reads and queued writes, so they cannot replace a newer expedition or revive presentation. Escape both cancels pending work and pauses active play.

The renderer, authored scene, simulation/world/content, economy proposal/checker, main entry and styles are unchanged. No later gameplay was implemented. Original [FND-01 evidence](FND-01.md) and both initial review reports remain historical and unchanged. No branch switch, delegation, push, PR, merge or parent integration occurred.

## Exact interfaces for coordinator reconciliation

`src/save/codec.ts`, schema **1**, content **`foundation.1`** and the five-field journal format/version/key are unchanged. Existing current/previous/preserved data remain readable. The original author's exported schema-1 save at `/tmp/siltwake-fnd01-smoke/valid.json` decoded with the corrected codec at tick **7513**. No migration or schema bump is introduced.

- **`src/save/writer-lock.ts` (new):** exports `SAVE_WRITER_LOCK = 'siltwake.save.journal.v1.writer'`; `WriterLockPort`, with `runExclusive<T>(name: string, signal: AbortSignal, action: () => T): Promise<T>`; and `browserWriterLock(manager: LockManager | null | undefined): WriterLockPort | null`. The browser adapter uses native exclusive `LockManager.request` with the abort signal. The critical action is synchronous. Unsupported locking returns null. Production has no in-process substitute.
- **`src/save/repository.ts`:** retains `LOCAL_SAVE_KEY`, `StoragePort`, `SaveSlot`, and `SaveRepository`. Its constructor is now **`new SaveRepository(storage: StoragePort | null, writerLock: WriterLockPort | null)`**. **`commit(save, replaceProtected = false, signal = new AbortController().signal): Promise<CommitResult>`** must be awaited. It validates/serializes before queuing and returns a detached saved snapshot. New `CommitResult` is success `{ok:true,value:SaveSlot}` or failure `{ok:false,code:CommitFailure,error:string}`. `CommitFailure` is `invalid | storage-unavailable | write-refused | lock-unavailable | lock-failed | conflict | protected | too-large | cancelled`. New `canWrite` reports readable storage plus a supported lock port; an actual write can still be refused. `load()`, `status`, `raw` and `backupText` remain synchronous.
- **`src/runtime/session.ts` (new):** exports `SessionConfirmation {title,detail,accept}`, `SessionEvents {changed,pause,entered,notify}`, `ImportFilePort {readonly size; text():Promise<string>}`, and `ExpeditionSession`. Constructor `(repository, events)` loads the slot. The app advances its public `state: GameState | null` only through fixed updates. Public session boundary: readonly `repository`; getters `busy`, `confirmation`, `autoSaveAllowed`, `persistenceMessage`; `newGame`, `continueGame`, `manualSave`, `autosave`, `confirm`, `cancel`, `dispose`; async `importFile(file):Promise<void>`; and detached `envelope():SaveEnvelope|null` for export. The app owns its lifetime. This module has no renderer or DOM dependency.
- **`src/runtime/app.ts`:** `SiltwakeApp` remains the composition/lifecycle owner. It injects the browser lock, wires session events, advances simulation, exports snapshots and disposes pending session work before presentation resources. UI action signatures remain unchanged.
- **`src/ui/view.ts`:** adds `persistence(message: string, autoSaveAllowed: boolean, hasSession: boolean, busy: boolean)`. It renders the warning, disables conflicting controls and exposes cancellation. `slot` remains unchanged in signature. Root `data-busy` and `data-autosave` are diagnostic presentation observations, not gameplay state setters.
- **Tests/config:** the test compiler explicitly includes `src/runtime/session.ts`; tests use a shared exclusion fixture only in `tests/persistence-support.ts`.

All source/config changes are confined to `README.md`, `package{,-lock}.json`, `tsconfig.test.json`, `src/save/{repository,writer-lock}.ts`, `src/runtime/{app,session}.ts`, `src/ui/view.ts`, and `tests/{save.test,session.test,persistence-support}.ts`. The only build-record edit is this new report.

## Production-browser evidence

Read both fleet and repository browser rules before browser work. Verified local T3 chrome-headless-shell processes on **factory-worker Linux**, never the owner's Windows desktop. Used T3 preview status/open, incognito storage and the owned production server `npm run preview -- --host 127.0.0.1 --port 5184 --strictPort`. Owned tabs were `tab_19_0430977b-1ed3-45f2-ac72-3683f9fe8942` and, after final keyboard self-review/build, `tab_1a_0430977b-1ed3-45f2-ac72-3683f9fe8942`. They were used sequentially.

Actual renderer: **WebGL 2, ANGLE / Vulkan SwiftShader Device (Subzero)**, Linux Chromium **154**, **1280×800 CSS**, DPR **2**, Rich canvas 1280×800. CPU: Intel Core i5-12400, six exposed CPUs. Original scene still reports **12 meshes / 79,005 vertices**. Actual screenshots were visually inspected: original island, reef ribs, waterline/pod access and readable menu/warning remain present. There are no renderer/art edits. This is software rendering, not dedicated-GPU performance evidence.

The following were repeated on the **final** `index-BMj4o6i9.js` build:

1. **Ordinary controls:** real New expedition, R cruise, Escape pause, F5 save, actual navigation/reload, Continue, Escape. Moved off the pod into swimming. Saved/reloaded exact tick **288**, position **`(0, -0.9815262744950862, -1.8115066308711003)`**, yaw 0. Readonly HUD/journal observations supplied the measurements; no game-state setters or fixture poses produced this route.
2. **Native-lock delay plus ordinary controls (diagnostic):** held the real writer lock in page diagnostic code while playing; real F5 queued a manual save and disabled conflicting controls. Real Escape cancelled it **and paused** at tick **325**. Tick and presented frames stayed unchanged, busy cleared, local bytes stayed unchanged, and native held/pending lock lists emptied after releasing the diagnostic holder.
3. **Actual quota, empty New Game (storage fixture):** filled only `fnd01-r1-final-quota` to **5,242,860 characters** until a real `QuotaExceededError`; reads still succeeded. Reload → real New expedition offered the fallback. Escape cancellation retained no session and no journal. Repeating and accepting created tick-0 session-only play, enabled a real export, and showed autosave disabled; no local record was created.
4. **Actual quota, existing-session replacement and valid import (storage fixture + ordinary controls):** constructed a legitimate one-generation journal from the ordinary saved tick-288 record (`previous:null`), then filled the named quota fixture to **5,241,360 characters**. This forces the next journal to grow to include its predecessor. A full quota alone is insufficient when a replacement shrinks the journal; an exploratory earlier attempt correctly succeeded for that reason and is not counted as refusal evidence. With the growth fixture, ordinary New Game and valid import each reached actual write refusal. Cancelling their unsaved choices retained exact tick 288, pose and whole local bytes. Repeating import and explicitly accepting entered the chosen tick-0 expedition with autosave disabled and export available; local bytes remained unchanged. The downloaded export's session ID and complete state matched the chosen file exactly (`b88dcb87-fb40-413c-ad6c-484627188a32`, tick 0).
5. **Invalid/future preservation:** real Import save/file uploads of malformed JSON and schema 99 produced distinct readable errors, no replacement choice, cleared busy, unchanged active tick 0 and byte-for-byte unchanged local journal. Repeated uploads used the actual Import control so its file input resets.
6. **Autosave disabled:** final unsaved exploration passed tick **7262** with the local journal unchanged and autosave still disabled.

**Cross-context native exclusion diagnostic:** two task-owned same-origin iframe contexts loaded the compiled production pure persistence modules; those modules were byte-compared to the final compiler output. Both independent repositories loaded the same real localStorage journal, then queued behind a real native holder. `navigator.locks.query()` showed one held exclusive lock and two pending exclusive requests using the shared name. One commit succeeded at tick 200; the other returned `conflict`; current/previous were **`[200, 1444]`** in the first run and ****`[200, 288]`**** in the final repeat. A subsequent write after rejection succeeded. A repository with no lock port read the local save, returned `lock-unavailable` on commit and left bytes unchanged; unit checks also validate its importable export. These are context/storage diagnostics, not ordinary gameplay or a claim to have forced a particular multi-process instruction interleaving. The deterministic unit test supplies the adversarial read/write-gap schedule. Diagnostic records were restored, native queues emptied and owned iframes removed.

## Remaining limits

No independent acceptance is claimed. Coordinator must reconcile these actual async exports before dependent consumers and freeze a revision for both fresh reviews. The shared Web Lock protocol requires all writing contexts to use this compatible build; an old build that ignores the lock cannot be made cooperative, so README directs closing older builds.

This pass does not requalify real host focus loss, hidden-tab transitions, graphics loss/restoration or unavailable-WebGL startup across browsers. Previous evidence and gaps retain their labels. Unsupported exclusion is directly tested through the injected boundary and browser context diagnostic; no full browser matrix is claimed. The remaining esbuild low advisory and main-chunk warning are disclosed. SwiftShader proves no dedicated-GPU frame-rate target. There is no human/campaign/ten-hour, physical rescue, M1 gameplay or economy-runtime acceptance in this correction.
